about: Plain-language summary of what the agent has learned about each person's tastes. Shown and editable under Settings on the calendar. When a person edits their summary, the agent treats every statement in it as correct and keeps it.

aaron.summary:
What I'm working from:
- Big yes: repertory and revival film — noir, Hitchcock, Lynch, character actors, sad and humane stories (you flagged the Kore-eda After Life revival).
- Electronic, experimental and ambient music and DJ nights at artist-run spaces (Junglist Heights, Halloween ATP at Current Space, John Berndt's night at the Red Room).
- Adventurous jazz in small rooms; DIY electronics and synths; photography and small galleries.
- Less likely: arena pop and tribute acts, kids-only programming, sports, pub crawls.

From your flags (29 Interested, none Not interested yet):
- History is your strongest thread: Doors Open, haunted-houses Profs & Pints, the BMI social night, the Clipper Mill Art & Industry tour.
- Art and exhibitions rank high: the BMA's Baltimore photography show, MICA's Globe Poster show, and The Stars light-and-sound piece at The Voxel.
- Talks keep landing (Profs & Pints, André Carrington's Audiofuturism talk), so Guilford Hall's and Red Emma's talks rank higher.
- Gardening and nature: Cylburn, Filbert Street Garden, Mushroom City.
- On trips, local food markets and craft fairs get a little more room (you flagged the Bioferia de Miraflores in Lima).

What changed since Monday: no new flags (still 29 Interested, 0 Not interested), so the picture holds. This run filled the thin late-December stretch with experimental, history and jazz picks: Circles & Moons, a solstice night of drone music and moon films (Dec 20), the Flag House by candlelight (Dec 19–20), the Tromba Marina Quartet at the Red Room (Dec 2) and New Year's Eve DJ nights. For Lima it added the Ricardo Palma book fair, gallery shows and Eraserhead at Espacio 303 (Dec 4).
